title: Sales Representatives of Services, Except Advertising, Insurance, Financial Services, and Travel
description: Sell services to individuals or businesses. May describe options or resolve client problems.

tasks.text: Attend sales or trade meetings or read related publications to obtain information about market conditions, business trends, regulations, or industry developments.
Monitor market conditions, innovations, and competitors' services, prices, and sales.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Consult with clients after sales or contract signings to resolve problems and provide ongoing support.
Inform customers of contracts or other information pertaining to purchased services.
Contact prospective or existing customers to discuss how services can meet their needs.
Distribute promotional materials at meetings, conferences, or trade shows.
Create forms or agreements to complete sales.
Maintain customer records using automated systems.

clusters.label: Performing for or Working Directly with the Public

tasks.text: Answer customers' questions about services, prices, availability, or credit terms.

clusters.label: Judging the Qualities of Objects, Services, or People

tasks.text: Compute and compare costs of services.
Develop sales presentations or proposals to explain service specifications.
Emphasize or recommend service features based on knowledge of customers' needs and vendor capabilities and limitations.
Identify prospective customers using business directories, leads from clients, or information from conferences or trade shows.
Negotiate prices or terms of sales or service agreements.
Quote prices, credit terms, contract terms, or fulfillment dates for services.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Customer relationship management CRM software
skills.def: Software to manage customer interactions. Examples: Salesforce software.

skills.name: Operating system software
skills.def: Software to provide the operational interface to a computer and provide higher-level services and APIs. Examples: Apple macOS.

skills.name: Sales and marketing software
skills.def: Software to manage, plan, analyze, or automate marketing campaigns, content creation, or social media interactions. Examples: HubSpot software.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: IBM SPSS Statistics.
